She kneads the dough with both hands until it forms a smooth ball.
A second splash of oil is pressed and folded into the dough.
The cook cuts the dough into pieces and rolls each into a ball.

The cook folds the strip into a spiral.

The lid lifts to show six dough spirals.
A floured ball is rolled out into a thin round disc.
The dough is flipped and rolled into a final even circle.

bible.story: The cook mixes flour and water, kneads in oil, divides the dough into balls, rests them covered, then rolls each ball into a thin circle, brushes with oil and flour, coils it into a spiral, and finally flattens the spirals into round rotis

beats.beat: The cook mixes flour and lukewarm water in a wooden bowl to form a shaggy dough.
beats.why: hydrates the flour so gluten can develop

beats.beat: Oil is poured in and the dough is kneaded into a smooth, cohesive ball.
beats.why: the oil tenderizes the dough and the kneading builds structure

beats.beat: A second splash of oil is worked in and the dough is finished as a single round ball.
beats.why: ensures the dough is supple before portioning

beats.beat: The dough is turned onto a floured mat, cut into pieces, and each piece is rolled into a small ball.
beats.why: creates even portions for the layered rotis

beats.beat: Each ball is pressed flat, rolled into a long thin oval, brushed with oil, dusted with flour, folded in half, and coiled
beats.why: the oil-flour layers and spiral coil create the signature flaky layers

beats.beat: The spirals are placed in a brown bowl, covered with a white bowl, and left to rest.
beats.why: resting relaxes the gluten so the spirals can be rolled thin without shrinking b

beats.beat: The cover is lifted to reveal six risen dough spirals.
beats.why: shows the dough has relaxed and puffed slightly during the rest

beats.beat: A spiral is floured and rolled out into a thin, even circle—the finished roti ready for the pan.
beats.why: final flattening turns the coiled layers into a flat bread that will puff when c
